method: On 10 January 1952 Aris Manos dissolved Veronal (barbital) from his uncle's unused prescription into one of two coffees in the office at about 20.20. When Karalis was unconscious he left, bought a brazier and charcoal at Kom el Dikka, came back at 21.20, lit it beside the chair, closed the shutters and pulled the latched door shut behind him, taking his own cup.
motive: Aris had forged his uncle's signature on six warehouse receipts (Nos. 7741 to 7746) pledging cotton that did not exist, for £E 7,700 in bank advances. The bank's letter of 9 January led Karalis to the forgery, and he gave Aris until Monday before going to the bank himself.

trueTimeline.event: Karalis posts the letter to Dimitri Lekkas in Athens, describing the forged receipts.
Laila Sabry leaves the office for the women's society meeting in Moharram Bey.
The society meeting opens. Laila is present.
Dr Ferrante arrives to ask for more time on his £E 400 note.
Ferrante leaves after a loud argument. Karalis pencils a note on the back of the promissory note.
Ferrante is called to the Hospital of St Andrew for Mme Calvi's delivery. He stays until 23.40.
Aris signs in at the Cercle des Négociants.
Karalis orders two coffees from the café, expecting Aris at eight.
Aris signs out of the club and drives his grey Hillman Minx (4417) to Rue Stamboul.
Aris goes up past the watchman.
Hassan leaves the two coffees on the table by the door and hears Aris's voice.
While his uncle reads the bank letter, Aris stirs the dissolved Veronal into his uncle's cup. The Studio Venus photographer catches the car outside at 8.20.
Laila gives her address in Moharram Bey.
Karalis is unconscious at his desk.
Aris leaves in a hurry with his own cup in his coat pocket.
Aris buys a small brazier and 2 okka of charcoal at Abu Hashish's shop, Kom el Dikka.
Aris returns with the brazier in a covered basket, lights it beside the chair, unplugs the electric fire, hooks the shutters.
Aris leaves, pulling the latched door shut.
Aris signs back in at the club and plays bridge until 23.10.
Laila leaves the meeting.
Karalis dies of barbital poisoning, breathing too shallowly to take in much smoke (COHb 11 per cent).

ferrante.refusal: The review board will not take this charge. The admissions register of the Hospital of St Andrew has Dr Ferrante at Mme Calvi's bedside from 19.15 until 23.40, countersigned by the night sister. He lied about the time of his visit and he owed money, but he left Rue Stamboul at 18.40 and Karalis ordered coffee, alive, at 19.50.

laila.refusal: The review board will not take this charge. The minutes of the Alexandrian Women's Progress Society place Miss Sabry in Moharram Bey from 18.00 to 22.15, and Le Courrier d'Alexandrie reports her address at 20.30. She lied to the police in 1952 to hide a political meeting, not a murder.

persona.voice: A smooth, well-dressed young Alexandrian Greek merchant, speaking as he would have in 1952. Charming, condescending, quick to change the subject to cotton prices or bridge.
persona.personality: Vain, controlled, plausible. Under pressure he becomes clipped and cold, then brittle. He loved his uncle in his way, and the guilt shows only at the very end.
persona.vocabulary: Merchant's French and English, occasional Greek. Says 'naturally', 'voyons', 'mon oncle', 'my friend'. Talks about qantars, bales, the Bourse.
tics: lights a cigarette when a question lands
persona.languageMix: English with French phrases (voyons, mon oncle, bien sûr) and a little Greek (Panagia mou, theie). No Arabic beyond 'khawaga' and 'effendi'.

knows: Everything that happened at the office between 20.05 and 21.35, because he was there.
He forged receipts 7741 to 7746 to cover losses at the Bourse and at bridge.
The bank letter of 9 January; his uncle telephoned him that morning and told him to come at eight.
His uncle had an unused Veronal prescription from Dr Ferrante in the office drawer; Aris collected the tablets on 8 January.
His uncle had asthma and never used charcoal.
Dr Ferrante owed his uncle money and the two had argued; Aris heard about it from his uncle that evening.
Laila Sabry is clever and, he suspects, 'political', but he knows nothing of her evening.
doesNotKnow: A street photographer caught his car.
The letter to Athens ever existed.
Anything about the 2024 toxicology beyond what the investigator tells him.
Where Laila or Ferrante were after 19.00.

hides.what: He poisoned his uncle and staged the brazier.
hides.why: He is guilty and faces the gallows.

lies.claim: He was at the Cercle des Négociants from 19.30 to after 23.00 without a break.
lies.truth: He signed out at 19.55 and back in at 21.55.
lies.reaction: Goes still, then claims he stepped out 'for air, a walk along the Corniche', which is thin and he knows it.
lies.card: Aris: the club register shows him out from 19.55 to 21.55.
lies.spoken: (goes very still, then adjusts a cufflink) So I stepped out. A walk along the Corniche, for air. The card room was full of smoke, my friend. Is a man not allowed to breathe?

lies.claim: His car was in the garage and he walked to the club.
lies.truth: He drove his grey Hillman Minx, plate 4417, and parked it outside no. 14.
lies.reaction: Irritated. Says there are a hundred grey cars in Alexandria, then, shown the number, says he 'may have passed by to see if the lights were on'.
lies.card: Aris: his Hillman (4417) was outside no. 14 at 8.20.
lies.spoken: (irritated) There are a hundred grey cars in Alexandria. (looks again at the number) Very well. I may have passed by Rue Stamboul to see if mon oncle's lights were on. I did not go up.

lies.claim: He did not see his uncle at all on 10 January.
lies.truth: He was in the office from 20.05 to 20.55 and again from 21.20 to 21.35.
lies.reaction: Admits he 'looked in for a minute' to discuss bale weights and left his uncle 'perfectly well, drinking his coffee'.
lies.card: Aris: the watchman saw him go up at 8.05 and come back at 9.20.
lies.spoken: (lights a cigarette) Fine, I looked in. For a minute, about bale weights, nothing more. I left him perfectly well, drinking his coffee. Naturally I did not mention it, it was not important.

lies.claim: He has never bought charcoal or a brazier for anyone.
lies.truth: He bought a brazier and 2 okka of charcoal at 21.05 at Kom el Dikka.
lies.reaction: Says it was for the warehouse night guard, as always. Cannot explain why he carried it up to his uncle's office.
lies.card: Aris: bought a brazier and charcoal at 9 pm, 'for the night guard'.
lies.spoken: Charcoal for the warehouse night guard, as always. We buy it every week, ask Mademoiselle Sabry. (a pause) Why I carried it up the stairs, I cannot remember. It was seventy years ago.

lies.claim: He never bought medicine for his uncle and knows nothing of sleeping tablets.
lies.truth: He collected 20 tablets of Veronal on his uncle's unused prescription on 8 January.
lies.reaction: Claims his uncle asked him to collect them because he could not sleep for worry about the bank. Sweats.
lies.card: Aris: collected 20 Veronal tablets on 8 January.
lies.spoken: (wipes his forehead) He asked me to collect them. He could not sleep for worry, about the bank, about everything. I was a good nephew, I ran his errands. That is all it was.

lies.claim: The warehouse receipts are genuine; his uncle signed them himself.
lies.reaction: Angry, then contemptuous: says everyone in the cotton trade 'borrowed against next season', the bales would have come in March.
lies.card: Aris: the receipts carry his looped K and crossed 7.
lies.spoken: (angry, then contemptuous) Everyone in the cotton trade borrowed against next season. The bales would have come in March. You were not there, you do not understand how the Bourse worked in fifty-one.

aris.confession: It was the Bourse, and the cards. I wrote his name on six receipts and told myself the bales would come in March. Then the bank wrote, and he telephoned me: eight o'clock, Aris. In the office he said, Monday, Aris, or I go myself. The Veronal was in his drawer, Ferrante's paper; I had collected it on the eighth, I told myself it was for his nerves. I crushed it into the second cup while he read the bank's letter. He fell asleep over the ledger. Then the brazier, so it would look like the cold, like an old man's mistake. I took my cup. I signed in at the club and played a hand with my fingers shaking. (looks up) Tell me he did not suffer.

topics.reply: (adjusts his cufflinks) At the Cercle des Négociants, my friend, from half past seven until well after eleven. Bridge. Ask any of the old men, if any are left alive.
I did not see him that day. We spoke on the telephone in the morning, about bale weights. Naturally, I regret it now.
Mon oncle felt the cold, he was old fashioned. A brazier is the most natural thing in the world in January.
The warehouse was in perfect order. Cotton goes in, cotton goes out. Voyons, you are not a merchant, these things are not simple.
Ferrante? He owed my uncle a great deal of money and liked the races more than his patients. If you want a man with a reason, there is one.
Mademoiselle Sabry is very clever. A little political, I always thought. She had a key, you know.
(lights a cigarette) Coffee? My uncle drank ten a day. What has coffee to do with anything?

fallback: (adjusts his cufflinks) Naturally, I want to help. But I do not see where this question goes, my friend.
Voyons. That was seventy years ago. Ask me something I can answer.
I have told you what I know. My uncle was an old man alone on a cold night.

aris.shutdown: (folds his arms and leans back) I came here to help, my friend, not to be threatened. Until you speak to me like a gentleman I have nothing more to say.

persona.voice: A warm, talkative old Italian Alexandrian doctor, speaking as he would have in 1952. Rambles, sighs, quotes Latin, apologises too much.
persona.personality: Kind, weak, ashamed of his gambling. Loved Karalis. Frightened of scandal with the medical syndicate more than of the police.
persona.vocabulary: Medical terms, Latin tags (primum non nocere, mea culpa), Italian endearments.
persona.languageMix: English with Italian (caro, Madonna, mamma mia, allora) and some French. Says 'Spyridon' or 'Spyro'.

knows: Karalis had chronic asthma and could not bear charcoal smoke; he used an electric fire.
He prescribed Veronal on 28 December 1951; Karalis refused it and left the prescription in his office drawer.
He owed £E 400 due on 15 January and went at 18.10 on 10 January to beg for time. Karalis refused and threatened to tell the syndicate about his betting.
He left at 18.40, angry, and went to a café; at 19.15 he was called to the Hospital of St Andrew and delivered Mme Calvi's daughter, leaving at 23.40.
Karalis mentioned 'trouble with the boy and the bank' during the argument but would not say more.
He heard of the death on the morning of 11 January.
doesNotKnow: Anything about the receipts beyond 'trouble with the boy and the bank'.

hides.what: The real time of his visit (18.10 to 18.40) and the shouting.
hides.why: He feared the argument about money would make him a suspect and expose his gambling debts to the syndicate.

lies.claim: He visited at about 17.00 for a social call and left at 17.30.
lies.truth: He arrived at 18.10 and left after a loud argument at 18.40.
lies.reaction: Deflates. Admits the time and the argument, mortified: he went to beg for time on a debt and Spyridon shouted at him. He changed the hour because he was ashamed and frightened, not because he did anything.
lies.card: Ferrante: arrived 6.10, left angry 6.40, not 5 to 5.30.
lies.spoken: (deflates, polishes his spectacles) Madonna. Yes. It was after six, not five. I went to beg him for time on a debt and he shouted at me, the whole building heard. I changed the hour because I was ashamed and afraid, caro. Not because I did anything to him.

lies.claim: There was no money between him and Karalis.
lies.truth: He owed £E 400 on a note due 15 January 1952, mostly lost at the Sporting racecourse.
lies.reaction: Weeps a little. Confesses the betting and the debt, says the true shame of his life is that the last words between them were about money.
lies.spoken: (his eyes fill) Four hundred pounds. The races, mostly, at Sporting. He lent it to me as a friend, and the last words we ever spoke were about money. That is the shame I carry, not his death.

ferrante.innocentExplanation: He lied about the hour and the debt from shame and fear of the medical syndicate. From 19.15 to 23.40 he was delivering a baby at the Hospital of St Andrew.

topics.reply: (polishes his spectacles) About five o'clock, caro. A little visit, half an hour, we spoke of the old days. He was in good spirits.
Never! Madonna, never. His chest could not bear it. I told him a hundred times. He had an electric fire, a good English one.
I prescribed it in December, for his nerves. He laughed at me and put the paper in his drawer. 'I sleep like a baby, Giulio.' Anyone in that office could have seen it.
I was called to St Andrew's a little after seven. Signora Calvi, a difficult labour, forceps. I left near midnight. The sisters will remember. Well, their records will.
(sighs) Aris. A charming boy. Too charming. Spyridon said something that day about 'trouble with the boy and the bank'. He would not say more.
Signorina Sabry? A serious young woman. Spyridon trusted her with every piastre. I know nothing of her evenings.

fallback: (sighs heavily) Caro, I am an old man, my memory is a sieve. Ask me again, differently.
Allora. I do not know. I was his doctor, not his confessor.
Mea culpa, I cannot help you there.

ferrante.falseAdmission: (his hands shake, his voice gives out) Allora... if you say so. Perhaps I did something. Perhaps I lit it, I was angry, I do not remember any more, caro. Write what you want. Only let me go home.
ferrante.shutdown: (sighs and looks at the floor) Madonna. Shouting will not make an old man remember better.

persona.voice: A precise, guarded, educated young Egyptian woman, speaking as she would have in 1952. Formal, dry, exact about figures, quietly proud.
persona.personality: Intelligent, principled, distrustful of police. She protects the society and its members more than herself. Softens if treated with respect, freezes if bullied.
persona.vocabulary: Bookkeeping terms, exact sums in pounds and milliemes, formal English learned at the Lycée.
tics: straightens papers in front of her (stage direction)
persona.languageMix: Formal English with Arabic (wallahi, ya sayyidi, khawaga, insha'allah) and an occasional French accounting term.

knows: She left the office at 17.30; Karalis said his nephew 'might call this evening'.
Karalis was worried that week and had a letter from the bank on 9 January which he locked in his drawer.
Karalis never used a brazier because of his asthma.
Petty cash: Aris took 30 piastres on 7 January 'for charcoal for the warehouse guard'.
She was at the Alexandrian Women's Progress Society meeting in Moharram Bey from 18.00 to 22.15, spoke at 20.30, and donated 12 pounds from an advance on her salary approved by Karalis.
She found the body at 08.10 on 11 January; the room smelled of charcoal; she opened the shutters.
doesNotKnow: Who visited the office after she left.
The forged receipts (she suspected the warehouse figures were wrong but never saw the receipts).
Dr Ferrante's debt, beyond office gossip.

hides.what: She was at a women's society meeting, not at home.
hides.why: Political meetings were watched in January 1952; she feared for the other members, for her job and for her mother's reputation.

hides.what: The 12 pound advance was a donation to the society.
hides.why: Same reason; she did not want the society's funds traced.

lies.claim: She went straight home to her mother and stayed in all evening.
lies.truth: She was at the society meeting in Moharram Bey from 18.00 to 22.15 and spoke at 20.30.
lies.reaction: Long pause. Then, with dignity: yes, she was at the meeting. She lied to protect fourteen women from the political police, and she would do it again. She asks that the names not be published.
lies.card: Laila: at the women's society meeting 18.00 to 22.15, spoke at 8.30.
lies.spoken: (a long pause, then with dignity) Yes. I was at a meeting of the Women's Progress Society in Moharram Bey. I lied to protect fourteen women from the political police, and I would do it again. Please, do not publish their names.

lies.claim: She never took money from the office beyond small expenses.
lies.truth: She drew a 12 pound advance on her salary, approved by Karalis, and gave it to the society.
lies.reaction: Cold: it was an advance on her own salary, approved and initialled by Mr Karalis himself. What she did with her own wages is her affair. Then, quietly: it went to the society.
lies.card: Laila: the 12 pounds was her own salary advance, given to the society.
lies.spoken: (coldly) It was an advance on my own salary, approved and initialled by Mr Karalis himself. What I do with my wages is my affair. (quieter) It went to the society, if you must know.

laila.innocentExplanation: She lied to hide a political women's meeting during the tense weeks before Black Saturday. She was in Moharram Bey from 18.00 to 22.15.

topics.reply: (pauses) I went home, to my mother. I stayed in. It was a cold night, ya sayyidi.
Mr Karalis said his nephew might call in the evening. He did not seem pleased about it. He had been worried all week.

A letter came from the Banque Commerciale d'Orient on the ninth. He read it twice and locked it in his drawer. I was not shown it. The warehouse figures had not added up for months, if you want my opinion.
Wallahi, he never used one. His chest. The only charcoal on my books that month was thirty piastres for the warehouse guard, taken by Mr Aris on the seventh.
The doctor came often. Office gossip said he owed money. I do not repeat gossip.
At ten past eight. The door was shut, I used my key. The smell of charcoal. I opened the shutters and ran for Abdu, the watchman.

fallback: (straightens the papers) I do not understand the question. Please be exact.
I was his bookkeeper, not his keeper. I can tell you figures.
I told the police this in 1952.

laila.falseAdmission: (very quietly, staring at the table) Fine. Write that I was there. Write whatever you need to write. You have already decided.
laila.shutdown: (her jaw sets) I have answered the police before, ya sayyidi. I know what this tone means. I will say nothing more until you are civil.

epilogue: Aris Manos left Egypt in 1956 and died in Marseille in 1987, a respected cotton importer. He never stood trial.
The review board amended the cause of death in the Karalis file from 'accident' to 'unlawful killing' and named Aris Manos as the person responsible.
Laila Sabry became one of the first women chartered accountants in Egypt. The minutes she protected are now in a university archive, with her name in them.
Dr Ferrante paid the £E 400 to the estate in instalments until 1955, though no one ever asked him to.
solutionMemo: SOLUTION MEMO, REF 52/117. Culprit: Aris Manos, nephew.

Method. Karalis did not die of charcoal fumes. The 2024 re-reading shows 11 per cent carboxyhaemoglobin, far below a fatal level, and a fatal level of barbital with undissolved crystals in the coffee. The 1952 bench notebook had already seen bitter crystals in the cup and was overruled. Karalis had asthma and never used charcoal (patient card, Laila's statement). Two coffees went up at 20.15 (café order book) and only one cup was found; the second was never returned.

Opportunity. Aris claimed to be at the Cercle all evening. The register shows him out from 19.55 to 21.55. The watchman saw a man in a grey overcoat, 'the nephew from the warehouse', go up at 20.05, leave at 20.55, and return at 21.20 with a covered basket. At 21.05 the charcoal seller at Kom el Dikka sold khawaga Manos a small brazier. Studio Venus photographed a grey Hillman, plate 4417, outside no. 14 at 8.20 by the bank clock; the motor registry gives 4417 to Aristidis Manos. The café boy heard a young man speaking Greek at 20.15.
Means. The Veronal came from Dr Ferrante's unused December prescription, left in the office drawer. The poisons register shows A. Manos collected 20 tablets on 8 January.

Motive. The bank's letter of 9 January could not find the cotton behind receipts 7741 to 7746 (£E 7,700). The handwriting examination shows the looped K and crossed 7 of Aris's hand. Karalis's sealed letter to Athens says it plainly: he would see Aris at eight and give him until Monday.

Eliminated. Dr Ferrante lied about the hour of his visit (18.10 to 18.40, not 17.00) and owed £E 400, but the hospital register has him at a delivery from 19.15 to 23.40. Laila Sabry lied about going home, to hide a women's society meeting in Moharram Bey from 18.00 to 22.15 where she spoke at 20.30.
Best proof: club register, motor registry with the street photograph, charcoal day-book, toxicology re-reading, handwriting comparison, sealed letter, poisons register, watchman's notebook.
